audits.title: New method to evaluate the practice of positive pressure ventilation in intensive care units.
audits.standard: Protective ventilation strategy; proportion of data points with unnecessary hyperventilation
audits.setting: Intensive care units at a teaching hospital and a district hospital (Oxford)

cycle1.result: Clear differences in practice between teaching and district hospitals.

audits.intervention: Intensive education programme with nurse-run simple ventilation protocols

cycle2.result: District hospital practice closely mirrored the teaching centre.

audits.citation: Roche RJ, Mackinlay C, McLaughlin A, Panikkar K, Young JD. New method to evaluate the practice of positive pressure ventilation in intensive care units. Br J Anaesth. 2003;91(3):419-420. doi:10.1093/bja/aeg193. PMID: 12925483.

audits.title: A complete audit cycle to assess adherence to a lung protective ventilation strategy.
audits.standard: ARDS network mechanical ventilation protocol: tidal volume 6 ml/kg ideal body weight and plateau pressure 30 cm H2O or less
audits.setting: Intensive care unit, Heartlands Hospital, Heart of England NHS Foundation Trust, Birmingham

cycle1.result: Tidal volume 9.5 ml/kg IBW; standard not met

audits.intervention: Implementation of a protective ventilation strategy and an educational programme

cycle2.result: Tidal volume 6.6 ml/kg IBW; significant improvement

audits.citation: Joynes E, Dalay S, Patel JM, Fayek S. A complete audit cycle to assess adherence to a lung protective ventilation strategy. Indian J Crit Care Med. 2014;18(11):746-749. doi:10.4103/0972-5229.144020. PMID: 25425842.

audits.title: Do we practise low tidal-volume ventilation in the intensive care unit? a 14-year audit.
audits.standard: Low tidal volume ventilation, 6.5 mL/kg predicted body weight or less
audits.setting: 15-bed general ICU, tertiary referral hospital (St Vincent's Hospital, Melbourne)

cycle1.result: Median tidal volume 8.15 mL/kg PBW (IQR 7.15-9.34), adherence 13.4%

audits.other_findings: Adherence better in more severe lung disease; overestimation of predicted body weight may have contributed.
audits.citation: Santamaria JD, Tobin AE, Reid DA. Do we practise low tidal-volume ventilation in the intensive care unit? a 14-year audit. Crit Care Resusc. 2015;17(2):108-112. doi:10.1016/s1441-2772(23)01050-5. PMID: 26017128.

audits.title: Protective mechanical ventilation in United Kingdom critical care units: A multicentre audit.
audits.standard: Low tidal volume ventilation ≤6.5 ml/kg predicted body weight; recommended PEEP levels
audits.setting: 16 intensive care units in two regions of the UK (multicentre 24-hour audit)

cycle1.result: Mean tidal volume 7.2 (±1.4) ml/kg PBW; compliance with low tidal volume ventilation 34%. Compliance with recommended PEEP 72%.

audits.other_findings: Mean tidal volume 7.0 ml/kg with volume control vs 7.9 ml/kg with pressure control (P < 0.0001); significant regional and unit variation.
audits.citation: Newell CP, Martin MJ, Richardson N, Bourdeaux CP. Protective mechanical ventilation in United Kingdom critical care units: A multicentre audit. J Intensive Care Soc. 2017;18(2):106-112. doi:10.1177/1751143716683712. PMID: 28979556.

audits.title: From a small local audit to a regional quality improvement project - Improving lung protective ventilation.
audits.standard: Tidal volumes of 6-8 ml per kg ideal body weight
audits.setting: Intensive care units in the Wessex region (SPARC collaborative)

cycle1.result: Adherence to lung protective ventilation variable across units (figures not reported).

audits.intervention: Regional quality improvement project: accurate recording of weight and height and a simple chart to calculate tidal volume.

cycle2.result: Average 30% higher duration of ventilation within target tidal volume (1843 hours of ventilation audited over both years).

audits.other_findings: Started from a local audit of weight recording and a regional survey.
audits.citation: Birkhoelzer S, Taylor M, Harris B, Adeniji K. From a small local audit to a regional quality improvement project - Improving lung protective ventilation. J Intensive Care Soc. 2019;20(1):53-58. doi:10.1177/1751143718777165. PMID: 30792763.

audits.title: Audit of low tidal volume ventilation in patients with hypoxic respiratory failure in a tertiary Australian intensive care unit.
audits.standard: Low tidal volume ventilation strategy as standard of care

cycle1.result: 92% of admissions lacked height recording; when height recorded 54% of ventilation hours were LTVV adherent.

audits.intervention: New electronic data-entry box for patient height (March 2016).
audits.other_findings: EMR change produced improvement that was not sustained; clinicians preferred multiples of 50 ml; poor adherence associated with higher mortality.
audits.citation: Wilkins D, Lane AS, Orde SR. Audit of low tidal volume ventilation in patients with hypoxic respiratory failure in a tertiary Australian intensive care unit. Anaesth Intensive Care. 2021;49(4):301-308. doi:10.1177/0310057x21993132. PMID: 34324389.

audits.title: Beyond audit: Embracing QI methodology to drive improvements in lung-protective ventilation.
audits.standard: Tidal volumes 6-8 mL/kg predicted body weight; target >85% of tidal volumes compliant by end of November 2019
audits.setting: Critical Care Unit, Royal Liverpool Hospital (UK tertiary hospital)

cycle1.result: Only 60.1% of recorded tidal volumes were compliant with lung-protective ventilation.

audits.intervention: IHI quality improvement methodology with repeated PDSA cycles and real-time data collection and reporting (specific changes not detailed)

cycle2.result: Sustained compliance with lung-protective ventilation for >85% of tidal volumes.

audits.citation: Watkin D, Welhengama C, Watmore J, Normanton R, Watson J, Wallis A, et al.. Beyond audit: Embracing QI methodology to drive improvements in lung-protective ventilation. Nurs Crit Care. 2023;28(1):21-29. doi:10.1111/nicc.12728. PMID: 34766423.
